history.period: Undocumented; described as a historic temple site
history.summary: Rudrapad is a historic religious site at Tezpur, Sonitpur district, on the bank of the Brahmaputra (temple lists place it near the confluence of the Jia Bharali and the Brahmaputra), housing a Shiva temple that draws devotees and tourists through the year. The name 'Rudrapad' is locally understood as the footprint of Rudra (Shiva). Documentation is thin: it appears in compilations of Assam's Shiva temples and in recent local reporting about the adjacent historic cremation ground, which is dilapidated and awaiting modernisation, with last rites often performed along the riverbank — an issue raised with the Sonitpur district administration. The site is being developed as a religious and tourist destination and doubles as a picnic spot. No foundation date, builder, or architectural details are published in the sources found; festivals are presumed (Maha Shivratri as standard for a Shiva shrine — specific celebration not documented). Coordinates (26.616247, 92.769395) are approximate, taken from a map pin adjacent to Rudrapad Temple, Mahabhairab, Tezpur.

name: Rudrapad Temple
town_description: Tezpur, headquarters of Sonitpur district on the north bank of the Brahmaputra about 175 km northeast of Guwahati, is one of Assam's oldest cities and a centre of mythology, archaeology and culture — 'the cultural capital of Assam'.

travel.railway: Tezpur railway station, about 5 km away
travel.road: West of Tezpur town on the Brahmaputra bank (Mahabhairab area); local road/auto from town
